Subject: Clarify Order Form: invoicing split / VAT handling

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form. A few quick items Procurement needs clarified before we can issue a PO:

- We need confirmation of how the minimum commit will ramp over the first 3 quarters (we typically need a month-by-month schedule).
- Can Redwood issue invoices split by legal entity (US vs EU) so our AP teams can pay the correct entity?
- VAT/withholding: if Redwood invoices from a US entity, we may have questions about VAT treatment and whether we should withhold – please advise what evidence you need from us (tax residency certificate, VAT registration).
- Preferred net terms: our standard is Net 30 for EU vendors and Net 45 for US vendors; can you confirm Redwood's position?

Could you send a redline or a proposed schedule and list any attachments you need from our side? We want to keep this moving; we have a Q3 kickoff dependency.

Thanks,
Elena Rios
Senior Procurement Manager
Vorago Inc.

Subject: Re: Clarify Order Form: invoicing split / VAT handling

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses and a proposed approach below; attaching our updated Order Form (Vorago-OrderForm-v2.pdf) with the ramp table filled in.

Proposed min-commit ramp (official schedule in attached PDF):
- Q1 (month 1-3): 25% of annual commit (monthly invoicing)
- Q2 (month 4-6): 40% of annual commit
- Q3 (month 7-9): 70% of annual commit
- Q4 (month 10-12): 100% of annual commit

Invoice routing / entity guidance:
- We can support split invoicing by entity. Suggested default routing: Redwood Inference US, Inc (for US invoices) and Redwood Inference Europe Ltd (for EU invoices).
- To issue entity-specific invoices we will need the PO to specify the invoice entity and the AP contact for each invoice.

VAT / withholding evidence:
- For EU VAT purposes, we typically need either a VAT registration number or a tax residency certificate depending on the transaction type.
- Please provide Vorago's VAT registration number for EU invoices and a signed tax residency certificate if you anticipate withholding. I attached a short evidence checklist in the Order Form.

Net terms:
- Our standard is Net 45 for enterprise orders. We can accommodate Net 30 for EU invoices as a concession if Vorago agrees to an early-payment credit schedule (1% for payments within 15 days). Happy to mark this in the Order Form if that works.

Next steps:
1) Review attached Order Form (Vorago-OrderForm-v2.pdf) where I filled the ramp table and added the invoice entity placeholders.
2) Confirm PO entity/addresses for US and EU invoices and provide VAT/Tax residency docs as applicable.
3) Let us know preferred net terms (Net 45 default vs Net 30 + early pay credit).

I'll follow up with Ben and Kimberly on the invoice routing diagram and DocuSign flow — copying them in.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com

Hannah — thanks, that helps. A couple of clarifying points from our side:

- For split invoicing: yes we can specify the invoice entity on the PO. Our AP teams prefer separate PDF invoices per legal entity rather than combined line items. Will Redwood do separate PDF invoices?
- VAT: we'll provide Vorago EU VAT registration and a signed tax residency statement. Is a scanned PDF of the certificate sufficient?
- Net terms: Procurement prefers Net 30 for both EU and US if possible. If Net 45 is mandatory for Redwood's internal billing, can you confirm the early-payment credit mechanics you proposed for Net 30? We need the exact language to review with Finance.
- DocuSign: please send the signing link when the redline/order form is ready.

If you can confirm the separate-PDF invoices and provide the exact early-pay credit clause, we can get the PO out within a week.

Regards,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming operational details from Revenue/Finance:

- Separate PDF invoices: yes, Redwood can generate separate PDF invoices per legal entity. We'll emit one PDF per entity with its own remit-to address and tax fields. See attached diagram (InvoiceRoutingDiagram.png) for how the line items map to entities.
- Tax residency evidence: a scanned PDF of the VAT registration or tax residency certificate is sufficient. Please upload to the secure ShareFile link (we included in the DocuSign bundle).
- Net terms and early-pay credit language (to be inserted into the Order Form appendix):
  "Net 30 (Vorago) / Net 45 (Redwood default). If Redwood agrees to Net 30 for a given invoice, Vorago may apply an early-payment credit of 1% of the invoice amount if payment is received within 15 days of invoice date. This credit will be reflected as a line-item adjustment on the applicable invoice."

- DocuSign: we prepared the redline and included the evidence checklist; please sign here: https://www.docusign.com/recipientSigning?doc=redwood-ordform-v2

Marissa from Legal is on copy for any final MSA/order-form redlines; Marissa, please flag anything material around the tax/residency language above.
